title: About East Coast Weekends | East Coast Weekends
description: Who writes East Coast Weekends, how trips are researched, how fares and opening hours are checked and how corrections work.
text: Home About About Weekends, planned honestly East Coast Weekends is a small independent guide to short trips from New York. No sponsored rankings, no ten-stop checklists, no invented fares. Independent Train-first Fares checked November 2026 How we choose destinations A place makes the site if the journey leaves enough of the weekend to enjoy it. We start with the train timetable, then build the two days around what is actually open, then check the cost of the trip end to end. How we check fares and hours Train times and fares come from the operator's own timetable and booking pages; opening hours come from the venue. Prices are the adult "from" rates checked on the date shown on each guide. Dynamic pricing means the fare at checkout can be higher. Independence No venue or hotel pays to appear. title: Atlantic City Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: An Atlantic City weekend from New York: the boardwalk, the beach and the casinos, with NJ Transit bus times and costs.
text: Home Destinations Atlantic City Weekend guide Atlantic City by bus Two and a half hours from Port Authority and you are on the boardwalk — the cheapest beach weekend on this site. ~2h20–2h45 by bus ~$40–45 round trip 1–2 nights Boardwalk, beach, casinos Journey ~2h20–2h45 by bus Cost ~$40–45 round trip Nights 1–2 nights Best for Boardwalk, beach, casinos Why go The easy beach weekend NJ Transit runs direct buses from Port Authority to Atlantic City. The boardwalk, the beach and the casinos are all within walking distance of the drop-off. It is not the prettiest town on the shore, but it is the easiest: no car, no parking, and enough indoor options if the weather turns. Steel Pier and the Absecon Lighthouse are the non-casino anchors. description: A Berkshires weekend from New York: Mass MoCA, Tanglewood and Great Barrington, with Amtrak and driving options.
text: Home Destinations Berkshires Weekend guide The Berkshires in a weekend Three and a half hours by train (once a day) or under three by car: museums, music and a countryside that feels further away than it is. ~3h30 by train; ~2h45 by car $70–120 RT train 2 nights Art, music, countryside Journey ~3h30 by train; ~2h45 by car Cost $70–120 RT train Nights 2 nights Best for Art, music, countryside Why go Culture in the hills The Berkshires pack a surprising amount into a small area: Mass MoCA in North Adams, Tanglewood in summer, and Great Barrington for food and shops. The Lake Shore Limited runs once a day to Pittsfield, so the train works if you plan around it. A car makes the towns and trailheads much easier. Base in Great Barrington or Lenox. title: Boston Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: A Boston weekend from New York: the Freedom Trail, Beacon Hill, the North End and where to stay, with Amtrak times and fares.
text: Home Destinations Boston Weekend guide Boston in a weekend Three and a half hours by train, then a compact city you can cross on foot: the Freedom Trail, Beacon Hill and the North End. 3h30–4h15 by Amtrak $80–250 round trip 1–2 nights History, walking, seafood Journey 3h30–4h15 by Amtrak Round-trip fare $80–250 round trip Nights 1–2 nights Best for History, walking, seafood Why go A city built for walking Boston's historic core is small. The Freedom Trail connects the main sights in a single line, and the North End is the reward at the end of it. Stay in Back Bay or near Boston Common. The train arrives at South Station and the T gets you anywhere else. Two nights make the weekend relaxed; one night means choosing between the trail and a museum. title: Cape May Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: A Cape May weekend from New York: Victorian streets, beaches and birding at the southern tip of New Jersey, with driving and bus options.
text: Home Destinations Cape May Weekend guide Cape May, at the tip of New Jersey Three hours by car and a different century: Victorian streets, a wide beach and some of the best birding on the East Coast. ~3h by car; seasonal bus Fuel/tolls; bus extra 2 nights Victorian streets, beach, birding Journey ~3h by car; seasonal bus Cost Fuel/tolls; bus extra Nights 2 nights Best for Victorian streets, beach, birding Why go The quiet end of the shore Cape May is the anti-Asbury: no boardwalk crowds, a historic district of painted Victorians and a beach that stays calm even in August. A car is easiest. Cape May–Lewes Ferry connects to Delaware, which makes a two-state loop possible. Spring and autumn are birding season; summer is beach season; the town is quietest in winter. What to do Three anchors One street, one beach, one walk. Town Historic district Painted Victorians, B&Bs and a walkable centre

title: Catskills Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: A Catskills weekend from New York: hiking, small towns and where to stay, with driving and bus options from the city.
text: Home Destinations Catskills Weekend guide The Catskills in two nights Mountains, small towns and a slower pace — but this one needs a car or a bus, not a Metro-North ticket. ~2h30 by car; bus ~2h45 Bus ~$60–70 RT; car fuel/tolls 2 nights Hiking, towns, autumn Journey ~2h30 by car; bus ~2h45 Cost Bus ~$60–70 RT; car fuel/tolls Nights 2 nights Best for Hiking, towns, autumn Why go The mountain weekend The Catskills are close enough for two nights and big enough to feel like a real break. Base in Phoenicia or Woodstock and let the weather decide the day. Without a car, the Trailways bus from Port Authority gets you to Phoenicia, and local taxis cover the trailheads. With a car, the options multiply: Kaaterskill Falls, the Devil's Path and the towns along Route 28. What to do Three good anchors One big walk, one town, one slow morning. text: Home Destinations Finger Lakes Weekend guide The Finger Lakes, if you have three days This is the longest trip on the site: four and a half hours by car. description: A car-free Hudson Valley weekend from New York: Dia Beacon, Storm King, Cold Spring and where to stay, with Metro-North times and costs.
text: Home Destinations Hudson Valley Weekend guide The Hudson Valley, without a car Dia Beacon, Storm King and a river town in one weekend — all reachable on the Metro-North Hudson Line. 1h20–1h30 from Grand Central ~$35–55 round trip 1–2 nights Art, river towns, walking Journey 1h20–1h30 from Grand Central Round-trip fare ~$35–55 round trip Nights 1–2 nights Best for Art, river towns, walking Why go The easiest weekend out of New York The Hudson Line runs along the river from Grand Central to Beacon and beyond. The trip is short enough to leave on Saturday morning and be in a gallery by lunch. Beacon is the practical base: the station, Dia Beacon and the main street are within walking distance. Storm King is a short taxi or bus ride away and is the reason many people come. Cold Spring, one stop south, is the other half of the weekend: a main street, a waterfront and a trailhead. text: Home Destinations Jersey Shore Weekend guide The Jersey Shore by train An hour fifty from Penn Station and you are on the boardwalk. The easiest summer weekend on this list. ~1h50 by NJ Transit ~$35–40 round trip 1–2 nights Beach, boardwalk, music Journey ~1h50 by NJ Transit Cost ~$35–40 round trip Nights 1–2 nights Best for Beach, boardwalk, music Why go The beach, without a car NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line runs from Penn Station to Asbury Park and beyond. The station is a short walk from the boardwalk and the beach. Asbury Park has the boardwalk, the Stone Pony and the restaurants; Ocean Grove next door is quieter and dry (no alcohol sales). title: Niagara Falls Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: A Niagara Falls weekend from New York: the falls, Maid of the Mist, Cave of the Winds and where to stay, with train and flight options.
text: Home Destinations Niagara Falls Weekend guide Niagara Falls in a weekend The one trip here that needs two nights: the train is slow, the falls deserve a full day, and the border adds time. ~9h by train; 1h30 flight + drive $140–300 train; flights extra 2 nights The falls, boat, gorge Journey ~9h by train; 1h30 flight + drive Round-trip fare $140–300 train; flights extra Nights 2 nights Best for The falls, boat, gorge Why go Plan around the journey The Maple Leaf runs once a day from New York and takes about nine hours. Flying to Buffalo and driving forty minutes is faster but adds airport time. Two nights is the minimum: one to arrive, one full day at the falls, one to travel back. Stay on the Canadian side for the view or the New York side for the state park; bring a passport if you plan to cross. title: Philadelphia Weekend from NYC | East Coast Weekends
description: A Philadelphia weekend from New York: Independence Hall, Reading Terminal Market, the Rocky Steps and where to stay, with Amtrak times and fares.
text: Home Destinations Philadelphia Weekend guide Philadelphia in two days The closest big-city weekend: history in the morning, market lunch, a museum afternoon and a walk along the river. 1h05–1h25 by Amtrak $40–150 round trip 1 night History, food, walking Journey 1h05–1h25 by Amtrak Round-trip fare $40–150 round trip Nights 1 night Best for History, food, walking Why go The most walkable weekend on the East Coast Center City is compact and flat: Independence Hall, the market and the museum district are all within a long walk or a short bus ride. Amtrak from Penn Station puts you at 30th Street in about an hour; NJ Transit plus SEPTA is slower and much cheaper. Stay in Center City and you will not need a car or a subway pass.
